nv_slot_club_wall.blurb: A small trad wall at the mouth of First Creek Canyon in Red Rock, sitting on the south side of Mount Wilson and facing Lotta Balls Wall across the creek. It holds 18 traditional lines, mostly crack climbs of one to three pitches, with plenty of wide cracks among them. Grades run mainly from 5.8 to 5.9, with a couple of 5.10s and a few easier lines at the bottom end. The sandstone is the typical Red Rock variety, and the wall catches direct sun through the winter afternoon. It suits climbers who like crack craft and a quiet corner of the canyon.

nv_the_promised_land.blurb: A remote limestone sport crag in the La Madre area west of Las Vegas, reached by dirt road and then a long, steep walk of about an hour. All 18 routes are bolted and the grades are steep: mostly 5.12 and 5.13 with one 5.11, nothing easy. The limestone is steep and tufa-streaked. Winter sun lasts until roughly mid-afternoon, while in hot months the wall is mostly shaded all day, though the walk in is punishing then. It is quiet compared with the sandstone of Red Rock and often breezy, so bring a warm layer for rests.

nv_dark_shadows_wall.blurb: The shaded north face of Mescalito in Pine Creek Canyon, Red Rock. It has 17 trad lines on sandstone, from a few moderate 5.8s and 5.9s through a solid core of 5.10 climbing to some 5.11 and 5.12 routes. Several are long multi-pitch outings, and one of the best known is often done only to its fourth pitch. Because the face stays in shade, it is an option on hot days but a poor choice in cold winter weather. Reach it by the main Pine Creek trail, taking the right-hand fork of the streambed past the canyon mouth.

nv_sweet_pain_wall.blurb: A steep sport wall near the second pullout of the Red Rock Scenic Loop, up a vegetated gully off the sand wash. Of 17 routes, 16 are sport and one is trad. The grades cluster hard: ten routes sit at 5.11 and 5.12, with a handful of 5.7 to 5.10 lines added more recently for lower grade climbers. The sandstone is heavily chalked and the wall is known for overhanging 5.11 climbing. It goes into shade in the afternoon, which makes it comfortable through much of the year. Parking at the second pullout is tight, so expect a short extra walk from the first lot.

nv_tuna_and_chips_wall.blurb: A longer sandstone wall at the First Pullout of Red Rock, reached by continuing up the side canyon past the Dog Wall. The 17 climbs are a varied mix of trad, sport and top-rope lines, with trad the largest group. Difficulty is mostly low to middling, from beginner-level 5.3 up through the 5.7 to 5.9 range, with a single 5.10. Several routes are multi-pitch, and a few are described as hard to protect or sparsely bolted, so it rewards climbers comfortable placing their own gear on easier ground.

nv_lake_mead_buttress.blurb: The easternmost big cliff of the La Madre Mountains, a dark grey limestone face of about 800 feet that looms over the west end of Lake Mead Boulevard. It has 17 routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus a few trad and multi-pitch options, ranging from 5.8 to 5.13 with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.12. It is a handy dry-rock alternative when the nearby sandstone is wet and is rarely crowded. The walk in is the weak point: flat ground first, then a steep climb that turns scrambly near the base. Helmets are wise.

nv_schoolyard_the.blurb: A cluster of broken sandstone cliff bands at the mouth of First Creek Canyon on its south side, in Red Rock. All 17 routes are trad and mostly short, with grades from 5.7 to 5.10 and a majority at 5.7 and 5.9, plus one easier line. The rock varies from dark varnish to pale, sandy stone, and most cliffs face northeast, so they stay fairly cool. The two sections are Coffin Corner on the left and Schoolyard Bully on the right. Allow about an hour from the trailhead on the First Creek Trail.

_expect.name: Texas Wall / West Velvet Wall, The

nv_texas_wall_west_velvet_wall_the.blurb: A big sandstone wall in Black Velvet Canyon, Red Rock, extending the Black Velvet Wall west past the Black Tower. All 17 routes are trad, mostly multi-pitch and some very long. The climbing is serious: a couple of 5.9s and 5.10s, then a heavy stack of 5.11 and 5.12 with two 5.13s. Reach it by the standard Black Velvet approach, about 40 to 45 minutes. Routes farther up canyon start from a terrace roughly 100 feet above the canyon floor. Expect committing days and rappel descents.
